correctness.rationale: The complement lemma s_b(u)+s_b(b^L-u)=1+(b-1)(L-v_b(u)) holds for arbitrary composite bases. Long division kn=j b^L+r with j<k<b proves reflected increment sum k-1-(b-1)(min(L,v_b(kn))-v_b(n)), including r=0. For b=p^a and c=v_p(k)<a the defect is floor((r+c)/a) for p-valuation remainder r, hence 0 or1; exact exceptional valuation counts telescope to (p^c-1)(b^L-1)/(b-1). Symmetry under n<->b^L-n fixes the defect sectors and proves the reciprocal Laurent polynomials. Pair summation yields (k-p^c)(b^L-1)/2 including F(0)=0. If b has at least two distinct primes, writing b=p^a m with p least prime implies m>p; k=p^(a+1)<b, L=2, n=1,m,b²/k exhibit defects 0,1,2, proving necessity. Domain requires b>=2, 1<=k<b, L>=1, 1<=n<b^L; no extension to k>=b is asserted. Algebraic derivations are exact.

originality.rationale: Dartyge-Luca-Stanica 2009 gives existence and density theorems on s_b(kn), not the exact finite-window complement-reflection orbit law. Dartyge-Tenenbaum 2005 gives joint asymptotic digit-sum distributions, not a published theorem in inspected material characterizing prime-power bases by a two-valued reflection defect. The complement lemma itself is elementary and is not claimed as unprecedented; the global iff prime-power characterization, explicit exception counts and sector reciprocal polynomials are the proposed new package. Potential classical digital-complement identities and distribution theorems remain a historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: Exact complement and carry identities may be longstanding folklore; the iff two-center characterization has not been checked against every older number-theoretic source.
